### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, only activities A04 and A07 were observed, each in all 200 traces, with A04 immediately followed by A07 (lag of 1 step) in every trace. [OCC001-004, DIR002, LAG001, POS003, POS006]
- In the later window, all six activities A01, A03, A04, A05, A06, and A07 appear in every trace, each exactly once. [OCC001-004, POS001-006]
- The order in the later window is A04 → A03 → A05 → A06 → A07 → A01, as shown by direct successor relations (A04→A03, A03→A05, A05→A06, A06→A07, A07→A01) and by pairwise order relations. [DIR001-005, REL001-014]
- The position of A04 shifted from the middle of a two-activity trace (position 0.5) to the first position (about 0.17) in the six-activity trace; A07 shifted from last (position 1.0) to fifth (about 0.83). [POS003, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process changed from a short two-activity sequence (A04 then A07) to a longer six-activity sequence (A04, A03, A05, A06, A07, A01) executed in every case. The new activities A01, A03, A05, and A06 appear in all later traces, and the order relations and positions consistently show the new sequence. The screening count (30 items vs 0.15 expected) rules out chance as an explanation. A competing explanation that the before window was a different process variant is essentially the same hypothesis; no other plausible explanation is evident.

Other differences: None beyond the structural change described.
